projects.title: offline teacher for village schools
projects.summary: A Turkish lesson assistant that runs with no internet, for primary schools in villages without a steady connection. Phones at night distil a 3B model into one small enough for a ten-year-old tablet.

projects.title: disaster message sorting
projects.summary: Reads the flood of messages after an earthquake and sorts them: trapped, injured, needs water, safe. Trained on the messages of February 2023, anonymised, so the next time the first hour is not lost.

projects.title: after the earthquake: translation
projects.summary: Turkish ↔ Arabic ↔ Kurdish for rescue teams and families in the first days, when no server is up. A 4B model made to fit on the phones that are already in the ruins.

projects.title: local history archive summaries
projects.summary: Summarises forty years of scanned town newspapers and council minutes into readable entries for the municipal archive. Istanbul first, then the towns that send their boxes.

projects.title: turkish lesson assistant
projects.summary: Answers a pupil's question about the lesson in plain Turkish and asks one back, for the evenings when nobody at home can help. Built on the open curriculum, checked by teachers.

projects.title: sign language captions
projects.summary: Turns Turkish sign language on a phone camera into captions for the hearing side of a conversation. The night work is the hard part: aligning thousands of signed sentences.

projects.title: behördenbriefe, einfach
projects.summary: Rewrites a letter from a German office into plain language, in German, Turkish, Arabic or Ukrainian, on the phone, without the letter leaving it. The phones at night tune the model on anonymised letters.

projects.title: night assistant for carers
projects.summary: For people who look after a parent at home: what to do at three in the morning, in their own language, with the guidelines of the Pflegekasse behind it. Trained on the open care handbooks.

projects.title: city archive, handwriting to text
projects.summary: Reads the handwritten registers of the Hamburg city archive, 1850 to 1950, into searchable text. Volunteers correct, phones at night learn from the corrections.

projects.title: interpreter for the jobcenter
projects.summary: A spoken interpreter for appointments at the Jobcenter, German ↔ Turkish ↔ Farsi, that runs on the phone of the person being interviewed. The night work aligns the vocabulary of forms and offices.
